q1: SELECT ITM.ITEMNO, ITEMPRICE.NP FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ITM.ITEMNO, ITEMPRICE.NP FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
counterexample: INSERT INTO ITP (ITEMNO, NP) VALUES (1, 10), (1, 10), (2, 20); INSERT INTO ITM (ITEMNO, TYPE) VALUES (1, 1);
explanation: Q1 first removes duplicates from the ITP table by selecting distinct ITEMNO and NP, and then joins this with the ITM table. Q2 directly joins the ITP and ITM tables without removing duplicates from the ITP table.
counterexample_dsp: A test case where the ITP table contains duplicate ITEMNO values, and the ITM table has a record for one of these ITEMNO values.
q1_validation_sql: SELECT ITM.ITEMNO, ITEMPRICE.NP FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2_validation_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
